'''Wendell Andre Carter Jr.''' (born April 16, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]].

==High school career==
Carter attended [[Pace Academy]] in [[Atlanta, Georgia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/wendell-carter-college-decision-official-visits-duke-kentucky-harvard-082316|title=Meet the high school hoops star who could spurn Duke and Kentucky to attend Harvard|publisher=Fox Sports|date=23 August 2016|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged 21.3 [[points per game]], 12.3 [[rebounds per game]], and 4.1 blocks while leading the Knights to a (27-3) record and a Georgia 6AA regional title. Carter would continue to develop his game during the summer of 2015 where he led his AAU Georgia Stars to a [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] Peach Jam championship title. Carter earned the Georgia Region 6 AA Player of the Year and second-team Atlanta Tipoff Club All Metro-honors. In his junior season in 2015-16, Carter averaged 21.6 [[points per game]] and 13.6 [[rebounds per game]]. In the state finals game, Carter scored 30 points and recorded 20 rebounds to lead Pace Academy to win the 2016 Georgia class AA state Championship. Carter was named an honorable mention All-American by the Naismith Trophy, a first-team Junior All-American by MaxPreps, the Georgia Class AA Player of the year, the Atlanta/South Fulton Player of the Year, and a first-team all-state selection as a junior. <ref>http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211644090</ref> In the spring and summer of 2016, Carter competed for the AAU team, CP3 All stars sponsored by [[Houston Rockets ]] point guard [[Chris Paul]]. He averaged 16.8 points per game and 10.2 rebounds per game on the Nike EYBL Circuit, earning second-team All-EYBL honoree. As a senior, he averaged 22.7 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 15.5 [[rebounds]], and 5.8 blocks while leading the Knights to a Georgia class 3A state championship on March 9, 2017. Carter was named Georgia All-Classification Player of the Year, Gatorade Georgia Player of the Year, first-team All-America honors from the Naismith Trophy, second-team accolades from USA Today, and third-team recognition from MaxPreps. Carter played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[McDonald's All-American Game]], where he finished with 10 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists. 

Off of the court, Carter was named the [[Morgan Wootten National Player of the Year]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18842896/wendell-carter-duke-blue-devils-recruit-wins-morgan-wootten-national-player-year-award|title=Wendell Carter wins Morgan Wootten National POY award|first=Paul|last=Biancardi|publisher=ESPN|date=7 March 2017|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/07/wendell-carter-morgan-wootten-poy|title=Duke signee Wendell Carter Jr. named Morgan Wootten Player of the Year|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=7 March 2017|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref> which goes to student-athletes who exemplify outstanding character, leadership, and academics. Additionally, earning a 3.8 GPA in high school and winning the school's Lance and Shield Award as a top scholar-athlete, Carter ultimately chose between [[Duke University]] and [[Harvard University]] due to their academics. <ref>https://theundefeated.com/features/wendell-carter-jr-duke/</ref>

==College career==
Carter was rated as a five-star recruit and the No. 4 overall recruit and No. 1 power forward in the 2017 high school class. <ref>http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211644090</ref><ref>https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/838</ref><ref>http://www.scout.com/player/189969-wendell-carter</ref> In November 2016, he committed to [[Duke University]] to play college basketball.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18120772/wendell-carter-no-3-recruit-2017-espn-100-commits-duke-blue-devils|title=Prized power forward Wendell Carter commits to Duke|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|publisher=ESPN|date=23 November 2016|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/five-star-big-man-wendell-carter-commits-to-duke/|title=Five Star Big Man Wendell Carter Commits To Duke|first=John|last=Watson|publisher=CBS Sports|date=23 November 2016|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref> Against the [[Indiana Hoosiers]], Carter had a double-double with 18 points and 12 rebounds despite being in foul trouble to lift Duke in a 91-81 win. <ref>http://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article188900019.html</ref> On the season, Carter is currently averaging 12.6 points and 8.7 rebounds. <ref>http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/4277847/wendell-carter-jr</ref> 

Following Duke's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Carter announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23201541/duke-blue-devils-wendell-carter-jr-declaring-nba-draft|title=Duke's Wendell Carter Jr. declaring for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 16, 2018}}</ref>

==National team career==
Carter was [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|named to the All-Tournament Team]] of the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]].

==Personal life==
Wendell's father, Wendell Sr., played professional basketball in the Dominican Republic after playing college basketball at Delta State. His mother, Kylia Carter, played basketball at the University of Mississippi. <ref>http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211644090</ref> Carter Jr.'s parents stressed academics to him from a young age, ultimately culminating in his decision to attend either [[Duke University]] or [[Harvard University]]. On February 23, 2018 Carter was 1 of 25 college players identified in an FBI investigation as having received impermissible benefits as a college athlete in that his mother allegedly had her lunch paid for by an agent nine months before Carter signed to play for Duke.  <ref>http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22553502/fbi-probe-corruption-reveals-basketball-powers-broken-ncaa-rules/</ref>
